===== #39 [icebox] 2026-09-25
Investigate using the macos JS engine instead of quickjs

https://github.com/madsmtm/objc2

QuickJS may be performant enough to handle frames, but it doesn't support internationalization. If there's no concrete reason to prefer quickjs other than a self-contained package, the bundled js engine probably makes more sense. It *does* add some risk, as the engine version differs with os version, but JS is extremely tight on specs and implementations.


===== #110 [enhancement,needs-triage,ai-drafted,low-priority,icebox] 2026-09-26
Measure a wipe in the pair's union box, not each layer's own box

**A wipe between two layers of different size does not meet at one edge.** The compositor measures the wipe's edge in each layer's OWN box (spec §7.5, `designs/spec/07.5-compositor.md:77-83`), so each layer's threshold sweeps its own rectangle. Spec §7.5 calls that "the price of every nested wipe working and the common same-size pair being exact". Canvas space was considered and rejected: it breaks same-size picture-in-picture cards (a 480 px card would wipe only between p ≈ 0.70 and 0.95) and nested layers. The measure right for all cases is the PAIR's union box (and the `clip_rect` frame inside a nest), which costs uniforms and nest plumbing (effects survey E1).

Checked at `976e674`: spec §7.5 still states the per-layer measure as the accepted price; nothing measures a union box.

This is an accepted limit a later pass may revisit, not a defect. Doing it means rewriting spec §7.5's sentence, the order-of-operations comment in `Compositor.metal`, and the recipe fields that carry the box.

**Done when:** a wipe between a full-frame layer and a smaller one meets at one edge across the union box, same-size pairs and nested wipes render byte-identical to today (`tools/proof/e1_proof.py`'s wipe rows), a new row for the different-size pair is made to fail on purpose once, and spec §7.5 says the new rule.

Moved from `designs/reelcut-remaining.md` §5d on 2026-09-26. Source: `archive/reelcut-effects-survey.md` §6 (E1), §8; ADR `designs/adr/effects-survey.md`, `designs/adr/roadmap-05-transitions-motion.md`.



===== #112 [enhancement,spec,ai-drafted,low-priority,icebox] 2026-09-26
Decide whether a left-hand media browser with bins is now due

**Reelcut has no left panel; media lives in an inspector tab, and a growing library has only search, sort and an "unused only" filter.** Spec §11 (foundations, "No left panel", `designs/spec/11-decisions/foundations.md:50-51`) says: "Media is an inspector tab. Revisit if libraries grow past a few dozen files." Road map 2's phase 8 added the cheaper answer first — search, sort, "unused only" and Reveal in Timeline in `app/Sources/MediaPane.swift` — and left a browser with bins until §11's trigger fires (road map 2 §4).

Checked at `976e674`: the §11 decision stands unchanged; spec §3 (`designs/spec/03-window-layout.md:58`) still says there is no left panel. Nothing records whether the trigger has been met.

Labelled `spec`: building it supersedes the "No left panel" decision, which is taken first. The trigger is a fact about real use (a project with more than a few dozen media files where search and sort are not enough), so it needs a person's report, not an agent's guess.

**Done when:** either a spec §11 entry supersedes "No left panel" with the browser's shape (where it sits, what a bin is, whether bins persist in the project and so bump `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`), and a follow-up issue carries the build; or this closes with a note that the trigger has not fired.

Moved from `designs/reelcut-remaining.md` §5d on 2026-09-26. Source: `archive/reelcut-roadmap-2.md` §4 ("A left-hand media browser with bins"), phase 8c; spec §11 "No left panel"; ADR `designs/adr/roadmap-02-ten-phases.md`.


--- comment (kpgalligan): **Batch triage 2026-09-29 (agent):** labelled `needs-human-review` — only the owner can say whether the library-size trigger for a left-hand media browser has fired (spec §11 "No left panel").

--- comment (kpgalligan): **Iced by the owner, 2026-09-30.** Nothing changes now, and spec §11 "No left panel" stands.

The trigger hasn't been observed: the owner isn't doing real work in Reelcut yet. The owner also noted that one person's use is a risky stand-in for the general user. So when this is revisited, the evidence should be real users' libraries (their size, and what was painful: finding, grouping, or seeing everything), not only the owner's. That evidence also decides between real bins and something lighter, such as media tags or colour labels, or a larger Media tab.


===== #119 [enhancement,spec,ai-drafted,low-priority,icebox] 2026-09-26
Effects E4: thirteen filter kinds and a clock

**Deferred by the user on 2026-09-15.** In the user's words: "we'll eventually add color grading and LUT import, but not now". Nothing of it is in the tree.

**E4 adds thirteen `FilterKind`s and gives the recipe a per-clip frame index and seed, so grain, scanlines and VHS can vary over time as a pure function of the frame.**

Shape (survey §6 E4; ADR `designs/adr/effects-survey.md`):
- `FilterKind` (`core/src/model_props.rs:289-298`, 7 kinds today) appends `posterize`, `threshold`, `solarize`, `emboss`, `edges`, `glow`, `directional_blur`, `fisheye`, `mirror`, `chromatic_aberration`, `grain`, `scanlines` and `vhs`. `Filter` gains `angle`. `MAX_FILTERS` stays 4 (`model_props.rs:259`) unless the phase says otherwise.
- The recipe layer gains `frame` and `seed`. The seed hashes the clip id (or the nest clip plus the inner id) and stays below 2²⁴. Today there is no time or seed uniform.
- Point kinds go at step 5 and `fisheye` at step 2. `mirror` is a second sample mixed by amount, not a remap.
- Every gather reads the RAW texture and must join `needsGather`, because a gather left out compiles out silently. `blur` and `directional_blur` on one layer are refused by name. Grain hashes on the canvas pixel, so it is screen grain.
- Output stays inside the layer's quad, so glow and aberration cannot bleed past it. That is a stated limit.

**First measurement (survey §5c):**
- each new gather's tap cost against the 8 ms budget (the fallback is one function constant per gather class);
- whether the specialization's dead-code cost crosses the budget;
- whether the spotlight lens can ALREADY carry obscured content out of a region (D7).

Depends on E3's shader headers.

**Proposed decision (a proposal, not a rule):** **D6** — every time-varying effect is a pure function of (clip, frame): a clip-local frame index and a seed from the clip id, never the wall clock or a previous frame. Echo, trails and true motion blur stay out. **D7** — nothing moves content out from under an obscure region. A remap or mirror hides a fragment if EITHER its own position or its colour's source position lies in the region. It is NOT in spec §11. It goes into `designs/spec/11-decisions/` (a new file for the road map that takes it up, with its row in the README), and into spec §1 where it moves a non-goal, BEFORE this phase's code.

**Concat is AGPL-3.0: none of its code, shaders, chains or colour tables may be carried over.** That covers design time and build time: no Rust, no `effect.wgsl`, no `effect.toml` or FFmpeg chain, no colour matrix, curve table, LUT data or other asset. A builder must not open Concat's files to "match" a look. Every number is Reelcut's own, chosen against Reelcut's own fixtures. "Concat's" means only the feature a person sees.

Checked at `976e674`: none of `flip_x`, `exposure`, `LookKind`, `VoiceKind`, `MaskShape`, `cutout` or `.cube` appears in `core/src` or `app/Sources`. `RC_FORMAT_VERSION` is 10 (`core/src/format.rs:173`, `core/include/reelcut_core.h:84`), so the first deferred phase to land is format v11; the survey's own v9–v15 numbers and op counts are stale.

**Done when:** the proposed decision is recorded in spec §11, the phase is built to the survey's shape (corrected against the tree), and its proof exists as measured output from the built binary, with each mutant from the survey's §6 E4 proof list failing.

Moved from `designs/reelcut-remaining.md` §5f on 2026-09-26. Source: `archive/reelcut-effects-survey.md` §4, §5c, §6 E4; ADR `designs/adr/effects-survey.md`.



===== #124 [enhancement,spec,ai-drafted,low-priority,icebox] 2026-09-26
Effects E9: Remove Background through Vision

**Deferred by the user on 2026-09-15.** In the user's words: "we'll eventually add color grading and LUT import, but not now". Nothing of it is in the tree.

**E9 adds Remove Background: a per-clip person or foreground cutout computed by Apple's Vision framework. No model is shipped or downloaded.**

Shape (survey §6 E9, §5b; ADR `designs/adr/effects-survey.md`):
- `video.cutout` is `{subject: person|foreground, feather}`.
- `person` uses `VNGeneratePersonSegmentationRequest` at `.balanced`, with a FRESH request per frame. `.fast` is stateful. `.accurate` runs at 1.7× realtime and needs 1.7 GiB per minute.
- `foreground` (`VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest`) applies to images and stills only. On video it flickered (up to 57 % of pixels flip between masks 0.1 s apart), so it was dropped there.
- A new `MediaImporter+Masks.swift` computes 10 masks per second of source, only for the windows clips show. They are 8-bit PNGs under `cache/masks/<media>-<subject>/`, made from the CODED buffer, under the stamp, marker and ledger discipline of `thumbs/` and `peaks/`. The compute device is pinned in the marker. Proofs compare against the cached masks, never a recomputation.
- **"No subject" rule, per CLIP WINDOW:** if no mask has at least 0.5 % of its pixels above 127, the clip draws UNCUT. Without it a screencast would be erased: person coverage measured 0.00 % on UI, text and cards.
- Compositor: the core emits `source_t`. Swift binds the nearest mask as `texture(2)`, sampled through `orientedUV`. The mask multiplies coverage at step 7. A frame whose mask is pending draws uncut.

**First measurement (survey §5b spike, `tools/proof/effects_spike/vision_*.swift`):**
- Calls are synchronous and need no TCC grant.
- Person masks are always 4:3: fast 256×192, balanced 512×384, accurate 2016×1512.
- Balanced runs at 4.2–5.5× realtime at 10 masks/s, about 16 MB of PNG per minute.
- Output is byte-identical on one device, but GPU and ANE differ by up to 25 levels.
- Segmentation misses backlit, from-behind and small figures.

Still owed as the phase's first step (§5c): the first-ever Neural Engine compile cost, and a mask-quality check on real camera footage by a person at the machine.

===== #125 [enhancement,spec,ai-drafted,low-priority,icebox] 2026-09-26
C2: a Reelcut-run relay for cloud captions, so a person needs no key

**Deferred by the user on 2026-09-21.** The product's plan is that the person supplies their own AssemblyAI key. The user deferred C2 until an integrated AI offering is designed (spec §11 R6-5's "Current product scope (2026-09-21)" note, `designs/spec/11-decisions/cloud-captions.md`).

**C2 is a relay Reelcut would run, so cloud captions work without the person holding an AssemblyAI key. It is blocked on caller identity.** A relay that spends Reelcut's AssemblyAI money must know who is calling. That needs a licence key, Sign in with Apple, an App Store receipt or a Reelcut account. None exists, and each is a road map of its own. A rate limit is not a substitute.

The designed shape (ADR `designs/adr/roadmap-06-cloud-captions.md`, "C2 — the relay"):
- **C2b, a bucket relay (recommended).**
  - The relay mints a presigned PUT, and the app uploads to the bucket directly.
  - The relay hands AssemblyAI a presigned GET, fresh at submit time and valid 24 h.
  - A webhook with a per-job secret triggers the fetch. The transcript is kept in KV for 24 h.
  - The object and the AssemblyAI transcript are deleted, and usage is metered on AssemblyAI's `audio_duration`.
  - It has no body limit and never holds the audio. R2 is the suggested bucket (no egress fee).
- **C2a, a same-protocol proxy.** It needs zero app changes (R6-6), but is limited by the host's body ceiling. That rules out AWS: API Gateway allows 10 MB and a Lambda URL 6 MB.
- **Protocol sketch:**
  - `authorization: Bearer <licence>`;
  - `POST /v1/jobs {bytes,seconds,content_type}` (401/402/413), then `PUT <upload.url>`;
  - `POST /v1/jobs/{job}/submit`, then `GET /v1/jobs/{job}`;
  - `DELETE /v1/jobs/{job}` as the acknowledgement.
- **Relay backstops:** a 24 h bucket lifecycle rule, a sweeper, idempotent submit, and never returning an AssemblyAI URL, id or error body unwrapped.
- **App side:** a `ReelcutRelayTransport`, with `CloudTranscriber` unchanged. Settings gains a Provider row and a licence field. The fake server grows the relay protocol, and proof rows 2–11 run over both transports.

Checked at `976e674`: R6-6 says a relay that must own the bytes is "one more `TranscriptTransport` conformer". **No `TranscriptTransport` protocol exists in `app/Sources`.** `CloudTranscriber` holds a concrete `AssemblyAIClient?` (`app/Sources/CloudTranscriber.swift:71`, `:84`). So C2b's first app step is introducing that seam, with `AssemblyAIClient` as its first conformer, as a pure move.

**Done when:** a caller-identity mechanism is chosen and recorded in spec §11, together with the relay decisions (C2a or C2b, metering, retention); the relay and its transport are built; and `tools/proof/cloud_captions_proof.py`'s rows 2–11 pass over both transports against the fake.

===== #131 [needs-info,ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-09-27
Opening a project whose media was moved fails instead of offering Relink

## Reported

When media a project uses is moved, opening the `.reelcut` fails instead of offering a way to relink it (reported by the user, 2026-09-26).

## What the design says should happen

Missing media is not an open failure. `readPackage` (`app/Sources/ProjectDocument.swift:527`) reads only `project.json`. A clip whose file is gone draws a slate, and `EditorViewController.offerRelinkIfNeeded()` (`EditorViewController+Export.swift:117`, called from `EditorViewController.swift:296`) puts up `RelinkSheetController` ("Missing media … Locate… / Relink"). `mediaURL(for:)` (`MediaDescriptor.swift:74`) tries the stored bookmark first, then the stored path.

## What did NOT reproduce it (build of 17ddac2, driven over MCP on a private port)

A project with one clip of `tools/proof/media/A.mov` (a copy), saved, the instance quit, then reopened with `open_project` in a fresh instance:

- **Case A, the file `mv`'d to another folder on the same volume:** it opens, and nothing is missing. The bookmark followed the move.
- **Case B, the file copied elsewhere and the original deleted:** it opens with `missing_media: [2]`, and `snapshot_ui window: sheet` shows the Missing media sheet listing `A.mov` with Locate….

The installed `/Applications/Reelcut.app` (built 2026-09-24) already has the relink code, which dates from 2026-09-05, so an old build is not the explanation either.

## Still to find: which condition fails

Not tested yet. Each is a candidate:

- The file on another volume, or on an external drive that is now unmounted. The bookmark resolves with `.withoutUI` against a missing volume.
- The package and its media moved together (for example a whole folder), so every absolute path is stale.
- Opening from Finder or File ▸ Open rather than `open_project` (NSDocumentController's own read path).
- A project with more than a plain clip:
  - a REVERSED clip. `ProjectDocument.swift:905` renders missing reversed assets behind a progress sheet, and a source that is gone may fail there;
  - consolidated media;
  - a recording;
  - graphics or captions;
  - a nest.
- What "fails" looked like: an alert (its text), a hang, a crash, or a window that never appears.

## Done when

- The failing condition is reproduced by a proof row: a project whose media is moved in that way opens, shows its slates, and offers Relink….
- The fix is in, and the row passes.

===== #374 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-10-27
Graphics: render SVG rasters deeper than 8 bits (supersede PR-5 for graphics)

Graphic clips are rasterized at 8 bits per channel (spec §11 PR-5), so a smooth gradient drawn by a graphic module loses its levels before the 16-bit-float compositor ever sees it. The owner wants the bit range of SVG rasters expanded; output dithering (the 8-bit exports) is being done first as a separate change, and this issue holds the deeper part.

## What was measured (2026-10-27)

The promo's intro graphic draws a radial gradient from `#0D1512` to a mid green over ~800 px. Along row 540, x 0–800, of a 1920×1080 `render_frame` PNG:

- green spans code values 23–65: 43 distinct levels, 51 steps, every step exactly one level;
- median flat run 14 px, widest 50 px: visible concentric rings, faintly tinted because R, G and B step at different radii.

The same frame decoded from the H.264 export keeps 41 levels (median run 10 px, widest 56 px): the encode is not the main cause. The steps are in the raster.

## Why it is 8-bit

- `graphic/` renders through resvg 0.48.1 on tiny-skia 0.12.0. tiny-skia's only `Pixmap` is RGBA8.
- Its highp pipeline already evaluates gradients in f32, and rounds to u8 at the store stage. Its lowp pipeline (u16 fixed point) runs whenever every stage has a lowp form, as simple fills do. It has no dithering (a `// TODO` about `dither_rate` in `pipeline/blitter.rs`).
- resvg's filters (`feGaussianBlur`, `feTurbulence`, …) operate on 8-bit buffers.

## What expanding it would take

1. A vendored tiny-skia patch: a 16-bit (f16 or u16) `Pixmap`, a deep store stage for highp, and forcing highp for graphics. Raster time will rise; measure it.
2. resvg's filters: patch them to the deep buffer, or document that a filtered region stays 8-bit.
3. App side: the graphic texture becomes `rgba16Float` (the compositor is already 16F, PR-1). The graphic raster cache (G-37, RAM/4 budget) holds half as many frames per byte; re-measure the budget and the prefetch (G-36).
4. A new spec §11 decision superseding PR-5 for graphics (text clips, shapes, stills and captions are PR-5's other 8-bit members; say which follow).
5. Proofs: graphics_proof and every frozen graphic baseline compare 8-bit pixels; they re-record or gain a deep comparison.

Payoff: banding-free graphics in the 10-bit and ProRes deliverables, and gradients that keep their levels when a graphic is graded, faded or scaled. For 8-bit exports the output dither (done separately) is what removes the bands, so do this after it.

===== #386 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-10-30
Speech duck: the release/attack crossing's bound ignores a next span shorter than the attack

Road map "audio" AP11 (ducking by speech, spec §11 AU-112), landed in 439c595 on `worktree-audio-updates`; left as a nit by the phase's second review.

**Where:** `core/src/audio_duck_speech.rs`, `speech_breaks` (around line 160):

```rust
let hi = e1.saturating_add(release).min(s2.saturating_add(attack)) as f64;
```

**What:** the crossing where one span's release meets the next span's attack is searched up to `s2 + attack`, taking the next span's attack line as valid all the way there. When the next span ends before that (`e2 < s2 + attack`, which needs short spans with Pre-roll and Hold near 0), the attack line is not the envelope past `e2` and the corner where the minimum changes over can be missed; the ramp across it is then interpolated between the neighbouring breakpoints instead of sampled at the corner. Only adjacent spans are paired.

**Fix:** bound `hi` by `min(e2, s2 + attack)` as well (and add a `duck_speech.rs` case with two short spans, Pre-roll and Hold 0, sampling the gain densely across the corner), or document the limit in AU-112.

Small audible effect at most: the multiplier stays between the two lines, so the duck is never deeper than Level.

===== #405 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-10-31
After a seek the live loudness meter counts the player's silent filler as the media at the seek's frame

Found while proving road map "audio" AP6b (the leveller), integrated in `bc885e9` on `worktree-audio-updates`.

## What happens

After `play_preview` seeks (any play not from where the stream starts), `MTAudioProcessingTapGetSourceAudio` hands each tap buffers whose `timeRange.duration` is zero (0/48000) and whose samples are silent (peak 0.0), but whose `timeRange.start` is the seek's frame. On a seek to 20 s: two of 4096 frames at 960000, then real audio from 963072 (logged per buffer on a Debug build, 2026-10-31).

`AudioTapContext.process` places the first of them in the live meter's ring (`meter.capture`, guarded only by a numeric time), so `LiveLoudness` sums 4096 frames of silence at [960000, 964096) and drops the overlap of what follows. Replacing those frames of the export with silence reproduces the meter's reading to four places (−23.2635 LUFS, against the export's −23.2532 over the same frames).

The first play after a build is exact, because the player's first filler carries an invalid time (`0/0`), which the capture already skips.

## How big

The error depends on the material at the seek:
- the off-mic fixture unprocessed, 12 s from 0 then 7 s from 25 s (loud speech): ΔI −0.0385 and −0.0398 LU;
- from 20 s (a quiet segment under the relative gate): 0.0000;
- levelled (the quiet segment lifted), 8 s from 20 s: −0.0102 LU on Release, −0.0041 on Debug;
- a constant pan −0.5 from 25 s (an earlier session): 0.0160.

## Tried and not kept

Not capturing a buffer whose duration is zero or invalid (a `sourced:` argument to `AudioTapContext.process`, false when `timeRange.duration` is zero or not numeric, and `guard sourced, …` before `meter.capture`) makes both seeks read 0.0000 and `audio_ap7_proof.py`'s L2 pass. But L3 (two plays of 2 s back to back, AU-72's pause and continue) then resets on the resume — "resets 4, 4, 5; from 48896 then 144511" — because the real audio resumes 5375 frames past the frame the sum reached at the pause, a gap the filler used to bridge. So the fix needs the resume path settled with it: what a resume's filler carries, and whether the frames between the sum's last tick and the pause were heard.

On the base's code the same Debug instance's `audio_ap7_proof.py` live rows read 2/4 (L2 "resets 2 -> 4", L3 "resets 5, 6, 6", one run).

## Where it shows now

AP6b's P3 (`tools/proof/audio_ap6b_proof.py`) subtracts a control — the levelled export played as a clip of its own — so the row holds the leveller's own part (spec §11 AU-67 (e)). With this fixed, the row could be absolute again.

`IsolationRenderer` renders each channel through its own `AVAudioEngine` manual-rendering engine in lockstep over one `RampSourceReader` (spec §11 AU-51). ===== #435 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-11-02
A get_media_analysis call that passes its wait cancels its job, losing up to one publish interval of work

When a `get_media_analysis` call passes `AnalysisLane.callWaitLimit` (60 s), it releases its owner, and that cancels the running job (spec §11 CJ-21). A job publishes only every 30 s and at a range's end, so whatever it analysed since its last publish is lost. Each "call again to continue" therefore keeps only what was published.

This matters for slow kinds: `masks` through the third arm on a Debug build (about half a frame a second), or long 4K windows. `shots` is fast enough not to notice.

Candidates:

===== #447 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-11-03
Auto Zoom: a Back left out under one frame lets a later cut take a stale pan's aim as its base

Found by CU7's review (road map creator-jobs, Auto Zoom). It landed in commit 6ce788bf on `worktree-creator-jobs`, and was not fixed there.

**What.** In `core/src/cursor_zoom.rs`, the CU-74 loop finds the placement in force at a cut. It takes the aim of the last landed action that ends at or before the cut, and sets the later given clip's base from that aim. This is correct only while every hold ends with a Back action, because a Back's aim is `None`.

But `plan_chain` in `core/src/cursor_zoom_visits.rs` leaves a Back out when it would be shorter than one frame (`if to - from >= timing.frame`). **Failure.** Take a run of clips continuing one source, and a click within one frame of a cut that closes the hold (for example, a cut into a given clip whose kept action meets the hold). The hold's last landed action is then the click's In or Pan, which has an aim. So that cut, or a later given cut in the same run, takes the stale aim as its clip's base: `plan_zooms` writes a `set_video` that the plan never meant, and does not close the zoom.

**Fix (the reviewer's).** Do one of these:
- Read the in-force aim only from holds that span the cut (`plan.holds`).
- Always end a closed hold with a Back marker, even a zero-length one, so that `in_force` sees `None`.

213	
214	When media a project uses is moved, opening the `.reelcut` fails instead of offering a way to relink it (reported by the user, 2026-09-26).
215	
216	## What the design says should happen
217	
218	Missing media is not an open failure. `readPackage` (`app/Sources/ProjectDocument.swift:527`) reads only `project.json`. A clip whose file is gone draws a slate, and `EditorViewController.offerRelinkIfNeeded()` (`EditorViewController+Export.swift:117`, called from `EditorViewController.swift:296`) puts up `RelinkSheetController` ("Missing media … Locate… / Relink"). `mediaURL(for:)` (`MediaDescriptor.swift:74`) tries the stored bookmark first, then the stored path.
219	
220	## What did NOT reproduce it (build of 17ddac2, driven over MCP on a private port)
221	
222	A project with one clip of `tools/proof/media/A.mov` (a copy), saved, the instance quit, then reopened with `open_project` in a fresh instance:
223	
224	- **Case A, the file `mv`'d to another folder on the same volume:** it opens, and nothing is missing. The bookmark followed the move.
225	- **Case B, the file copied elsewhere and the original deleted:** it opens with `missing_media: [2]`, and `snapshot_ui window: sheet` shows the Missing media sheet listing `A.mov` with Locate….
226	
227	The installed `/Applications/Reelcut.app` (built 2026-09-24) already has the relink code, which dates from 2026-09-05, so an old build is not the explanation either.
228	
229	## Still to find: which condition fails
230	
231	Not tested yet. Each is a candidate:
232	
233	- The file on another volume, or on an external drive that is now unmounted. The bookmark resolves with `.withoutUI` against a missing volume.
234	- The package and its media moved together (for example a whole folder), so every absolute path is stale.
235	- Opening from Finder or File ▸ Open rather than `open_project` (NSDocumentController's own read path).
236	- A project with more than a plain clip:
237	  - a REVERSED clip. `ProjectDocument.swift:905` renders missing reversed assets behind a progress sheet, and a source that is gone may fail there;
238	  - consolidated media;
239	  - a recording;
240	  - graphics or captions;
241	  - a nest.
242	- What "fails" looked like: an alert (its text), a hang, a crash, or a window that never appears.
243

171	Graphics: render SVG rasters deeper than 8 bits (supersede PR-5 for graphics)
172	
173	Graphic clips are rasterized at 8 bits per channel (spec §11 PR-5), so a smooth gradient drawn by a graphic module loses its levels before the 16-bit-float compositor ever sees it. The owner wants the bit range of SVG rasters expanded; output dithering (the 8-bit exports) is being done first as a separate change, and this issue holds the deeper part.
174	
175	## What was measured (2026-10-27)
176	
177	The promo's intro graphic draws a radial gradient from `#0D1512` to a mid green over ~800 px. Along row 540, x 0–800, of a 1920×1080 `render_frame` PNG:
178	
179	- green spans code values 23–65: 43 distinct levels, 51 steps, every step exactly one level;
180	- median flat run 14 px, widest 50 px: visible concentric rings, faintly tinted because R, G and B step at different radii.
181	
182	The same frame decoded from the H.264 export keeps 41 levels (median run 10 px, widest 56 px): the encode is not the main cause. The steps are in the raster.
183	
184	## Why it is 8-bit
185	
186	- `graphic/` renders through resvg 0.48.1 on tiny-skia 0.12.0. tiny-skia's only `Pixmap` is RGBA8.
187	- Its highp pipeline already evaluates gradients in f32, and rounds to u8 at the store stage. Its lowp pipeline (u16 fixed point) runs whenever every stage has a lowp form, as simple fills do. It has no dithering (a `// TODO` about `dither_rate` in `pipeline/blitter.rs`).
188	- resvg's filters (`feGaussianBlur`, `feTurbulence`, …) operate on 8-bit buffers.
189	
190	## What expanding it would take
191	
192	1. A vendored tiny-skia patch: a 16-bit (f16 or u16) `Pixmap`, a deep store stage for highp, and forcing highp for graphics. Raster time will rise; measure it.
193	2. resvg's filters: patch them to the deep buffer, or document that a filtered region stays 8-bit.
194	3. App side: the graphic texture becomes `rgba16Float` (the compositor is already 16F, PR-1). The graphic raster cache (G-37, RAM/4 budget) holds half as many frames per byte; re-measure the budget and the prefetch (G-36).
195	4. A new spec §11 decision superseding PR-5 for graphics (text clips, shapes, stills and captions are PR-5's other 8-bit members; say which follow).
196	5. Proofs: graphics_proof and every frozen graphic baseline compare 8-bit pixels; they re-record or gain a deep comparison.
197	
198	Payoff: banding-free graphics in the 10-bit and ProRes deliverables, and gradients that keep their levels when a graphic is graded, faded or scaled. For 8-bit exports the output dither (done separately) is what removes the bands, so do this after it.

# Open issues ready to work — 2026-11-08

110 open issues on kpgalligan/framejob, each read and the claims spot-checked
against main at a0bae333. "Ready" means: the issue names the defect or the
feature precisely, names where it lives, names a fix or an acceptance, needs
no owner answer, and depends on nothing that is absent from the tree.

Every creator-jobs and audio commit the issues cite is on main. The one branch
that is not is `worktree-tutorial-handler` (e3169260), which blocks #425 and #426.

| 456 | Switch by Speaker faces mode: empty range adds a spurious no-face refusal; a marker range past the grid forms a crossed `ClosedRange` and TRAPS (same pattern in `AnalysisMasks.swift:151`) | `count > 0` in the where clause; `guard lo <= hi`; probe rows | S, app |

| 444 | Transcript tab keeps an old voice cache for a cloud-transcribed media until the tab is hidden and shown | One line in `cacheLanded`; `TranscriptTabSource.swift` is at 598 so a pure move first | S, app |

### Stage 0 — triage (`lc-triage`) — always runs

- Run mutants for the decisions the batch adds.
- `make gate` ONCE when the code is complete, in the foreground (Bash timeout 600000). Three lanes share the machine, so it can run past the 600 s cap; a re-run skips what already passed, so run it again rather than backgrounding it.
- Run the batch's proof once against Release (`RC_PROOF_APP=release`, after the gate's `make app`).
- Record each command and its result. A number in a record is written only when a run printed it, and a control is called a control.
- Timing is noisy with three lanes running. Repeat a timing-sensitive measurement and say how many runs it took.

### For the adversary and the reviewer

- **Adversary:** treat `00-repro.md` as a claim, not a fact. Read the scripts in `$HANDOFF/repro/`. A row called `confirmed` that didn't run the issue's steps, ran in less than it says, or tested something else is an objection. So is a fix planned for a `not-reproduced` or `reading` row, a filed behaviour spec §11 records as deliberate (unless an owner answer changes it), and a plan that departs from `owner-answers.md`.
- **Reviewer:** a fix with no proof row red on the base app is a blocker, and so is a docs page that still states the old behaviour, and so is a departure from `owner-answers.md`.

### Commits

The implementer and fixers COMMIT on their worktree's branch, naming paths explicitly, with a plain message. A pure move goes first in its own commit, with a subject starting `Pure move:`. Never commit `FrameJob.xcodeproj`, `tools/proof/work/`, `tools/proof/media/` or build products. Return the base sha (`main`'s HEAD when the worktree started), the tip sha and the worktree path. The integrator turns the range into one commit. A commit can take a few minutes to return: the repo's post-commit hook runs `entire`. Wait for it, and don't kill it.

### Things never to do

- **Never open, print, grep or list anything under `.secrets/`.** Never spend money: no `--live` proof, no paid call. The assistant is driven only against its stand-in server.
- **Never run Copy or Cut through the menu**, and never write to the general pasteboard: it overwrites the owner's clipboard. Use a probe that keeps to a private pasteboard, or say `cannot-run`.
- **Never perform a persisting menu item** on any build (View ▸ Snapping, Safe Areas, Hide Inspector, Timeline Track Height, Preview Quality).
- **Never take the Mac's focus or put a window in front of the owner.** No `open`, no `osascript`, no System Events, no posted CGEvents.
- **Kill only a pid you launched.** The owner's own Frame Job, any other session's instance and any dev server you didn't start are left alone.
- The Concat rule stands: none of its code, shaders, chains or colour tables.

# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

# Binding for every stage of the "fixes" batches (2026-11-09)

The owner, 2026-11-09: "Start fixing everything in 'Defects with a fix already named in the issue'. Use 3 lanes to fix issues in parallel. Try to batch issues where feasible. Use /litecode for implementation."

The issues are review nits and defects filed by earlier road maps. Each names its file, its failure and a fix, and on 2026-11-08 the code site each one names was found still present on main at a0bae333. The named fix is a lead, not an order: read the code, confirm the failure by a test, probe or MCP row, and build the fix that is right for the code as it stands. Read each issue with `gh issue view <N> --comments`.

Where an issue cites `docs/guide/…`, that guide is retired: the documentation site in `docs/site/` is where the behaviour is documented now (`docs/site/CLAUDE.md` is its rulebook). Where an issue cites a road map record in `designs/<name>.md`, it is archived under `archive/` and condensed in `designs/adr/`.

### Where to work

- **The integration worktree** is I = `/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-int`, branch `fixes-int`. It is kept equal to `main` between landings.
  - Only the integrator writes there. Everyone else reads it at most.
  - Never touch the main checkout `/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob`. The integrator alone fast-forwards `main` to I. Never push.
  - Never touch another lane's worktree.
- **The implementer and every fixer run in a worktree of their own.** It is your current working directory when you start; the harness made it from `main`'s HEAD, which holds every batch landed so far.
  - Before building, CoW-copy I's caches so the build is not cold. Skip any that are absent:
    - `cp -cR /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-int/build ./build`
    - `cp -cR /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-int/core/target ./core/target`
    - `cp -cR /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-int/graphic/target ./graphic/target`
    - `cp -cR /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-int/mcp-proxy/target ./mcp-proxy/target`
    - `cp -cR /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-int/agent/node_modules ./agent/node_modules`
    - `cp -cR /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-int/tools/proof/media ./tools/proof/media`
    - `cp -cR /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-int/docs/site/node_modules ./docs/site/node_modules`
  - A fixer copies these from the previous stage's worktree instead; it is told which.
  - Use absolute paths inside your own worktree. Write a multi-step shell sequence to a script file in your scratch folder and run it as one command.
- The designer, adversary and reviewer read code in I (read-only).
- **Scratch files** go in a subfolder of the scratchpad named after your batch and stage, never its root. Three lanes share it.

### Owner questions

A decision in spec §11 is not re-litigated. A fix that needs a new decision, or amends one (several issues say "or amend AU-nn to say so"), records it in the newest suitable file in `designs/spec/11-decisions/` with its index row, BEFORE the code. Where an issue offers "fix the code OR record the limit", prefer fixing the code unless the fix is disproportionate; say which you chose and why. If a fix needs a genuine owner choice (a trade-off between behaviours the owner would notice, dropping something they asked for), do not choose:

- If it holds back only some issues, list them in the spec under `## Held for the owner`, each with the question, the options and your recommendation, and go on without them.
- Only if nothing in the batch can proceed, write `STOP: <the question, the options, your recommendation>` at the top of your output.

### Fixes

- **Each fix gets a check that is red without it and green with it.** A core change gets a test in `core/tests/`. An app change gets a probe row (through `tools/proof/swift_build.py`) or an MCP proof row in the area's existing proof in `tools/proof/`, not a throwaway. Then prove red: apply a mutant that restores the old behaviour at the fix's site, run the row, record that it fails, and revert the mutant. A row that was never seen red proves nothing. Record both results in `04-checks.txt`.
- A user-visible change follows the root CLAUDE.md's recipe: spec §5.2/§6/§7.9 for anything they mirror, and an MCP mirror for every user-visible edit. The parity check stays clean. A text the fix changes on the site (`docs/site/`) is updated with it, and `python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` run.
- A persisted field bumps `RC_FORMAT_VERSION` and the header, with a `schema_vN.rs`. None of this round's issues should need one; say so if one does.
- A check only a person can make is a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`, in the same change.
- **File size:** a file at ~600 lines gives something up before it takes anything on, by a pure move committed alone (`TranscriptTabSource.swift` at 598 and `AnalysisFrames.swift` at 409 are named by their issues). New files are capped at 400 lines. Frozen files take wiring only. Never run `xcodegen` bare; use `make project`.
- **Residue rule:** a problem the batch uncovers in code it is in is fixed in the batch. Only work that needs the owner, or is as big as the batch, goes under "To file" in your notes, with a draft title and body.
- **Never edit any CLAUDE.md.** List each edit needed under "CLAUDE.md edits owed", with the exact text. The integrator applies them. `docs/site/CLAUDE.md` included.

### Verification

Follows the root CLAUDE.md's "Verification" section.

- Targeted tests and probes in the loop. `make typecheck` after Swift edits: 0 errors and exactly the 4 baseline warnings. `make lint` and `cargo fmt` after Rust edits.
- `make app-debug` before driving the app. Launch your own instance with `python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch`, and stop only that pid. `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log` must print nothing before you trust a run.
- Mutants for the decisions the batch adds (the red/green rule above covers each fix's own).
- `make gate` ONCE when the code is complete, in the foreground (Bash timeout 600000). Three lanes share the machine, so it can run past the 600 s cap; a re-run skips what already passed, so run it again rather than backgrounding it.
- Any MCP proof the batch adds rows to runs once against Release (`RC_PROOF_APP=release`, after the gate's `make app`).
- Record each command and its result. A number in a record is written only when a run printed it.

### For the adversary and the reviewer

- **Adversary:** a fix planned without a red/green check is an objection; so is a plan that re-litigates a spec §11 decision, or that records a limit where a fix was cheap, or that fixes the issue's named line without reading whether the code around it has moved since the issue was filed.
- **Reviewer:** a fix with no row seen red is a blocker; so is a site page that still states the old behaviour, a parity complaint, or a fifth typecheck warning.

The implementer and fixers COMMIT on their worktree's branch, naming paths explicitly, with a plain message. A pure move goes first in its own commit, with a subject starting `Pure move:`. Never commit `FrameJob.xcodeproj`, `tools/proof/work/`, `tools/proof/media/` or build products. Return the base sha (`main`'s HEAD when the worktree started), the tip sha and the worktree path. The integrator turns the range into one commit (pure moves excepted). A commit can take a few minutes to return: the repo's post-commit hook runs `entire`. Wait for it, and don't kill it.

- **Never open, print, grep or list anything under `.secrets/`.** Never spend money: no `--live` proof, no paid call.
- **Never run Copy or Cut through the menu**, and never write to the general pasteboard.
- **Never perform a persisting menu item** on any build (View ▸ Snapping, Safe Areas, Hide Inspector, Timeline Track Height, Preview Quality).
- **Never take the Mac's focus or put a window in front of the owner.** No `open`, no `osascript`, no System Events, no posted CGEvents.

- The Concat rule stands: none of its code, shaders, chains or colour tables.

The three lanes are running. Here is what's in flight and how it is set up.

**The round**

All 26 issues from the report's first section are split into seven batches by area, so no two lanes touch the same files:

- **Lane A, audio inspector:** a1 #392 #407 #406 #400 #401 #413, then a2 #410 #411 #412 #409 #397.
- **Lane B, core and readers:** b1 #447 #398 #386 #394 #393, then b2 #435 #437, then b3 #369 (the reader audit, broadest, so it lands last).
- **Lane C, creator-jobs app side:** c1 #456 #457 #460 #458 #459, then c2 #444 #438.

Each batch goes through litecode's full pipeline (triage, design, adversary, implement, review and fix loop), then a serialized integrator cherry-picks it onto the integration worktree `~/devel/framejob-int`, runs `make gate`, fast-forwards main, regenerates the Xcode project in the main checkout, and comments on and closes the issues. Nothing is pushed.

**Rules this round adds**

- Every fix needs a check seen red without it and green with it: a core test or a probe or proof row, with a mutant restoring the old code to show the red. There is no frozen base app this time.
- Where an issue offers "fix the code or record the limit", the lanes prefer the fix and say why.
- Issues pointing at the retired `docs/guide/` are redirected to the documentation site. Part 2 of #457 is already fixed on the site, so only its argument-order half is in scope.

**State and recovery**

The binding rules, lane split and workflow ids are in `~/.claude/litecode/framejob/fixes/STATE.md`, and I saved a memory pointing there. A failed batch does not stop its lane. I'll report when the workflow finishes, with each batch's commit and any issue held for your decision.

#394 is fixed and main is pushed. All 26 issues from the report's first section are now closed.

**#394, commit 584ca26e.** The `unicode-normalization` crate is in the core, and stem names compare decomposed, lowercased, then recomposed. The adversary stage caught a real gap in the first design: NFC then lowercase misses letters that only have a precomposed lowercase form, such as ǰ against J plus a combining caron, which APFS treats as one file name. The final order handles those. The test has three cases, was red before the fix and under both mutants, and green after. Spec §11 AU-108, §7.8, §7.10 and the site's stems page say the new rule, and the acknowledgements pick up the crate's licences. Gate passed.

**Pushed:** main a0bae333..584ca26e, ten commits, all seven lane batches plus this one.

**Cleaned up:** the integration worktree and its branch are removed. Only the locked tutorial-handler worktree remains. Disk is at 134 GB free.
